content:
maria: heads up — ran the new quantized-llama-v2 onboard eval and weird thing: holdout recall jumped ~6% but manual spot-check shows obvious leakage.
kevin: ugh. any repro steps or logs?
maria: repro is in the eval-runner CI artifact. main red flag is a tiny list of holdout ids showing up in the top predictions repeatedly. pasted snippet:
```
# eval summary (quantized artifact)
holdout_dupes: ["uid_412", "uid_412", "uid_889", "uid_412"]
precision@1: 0.82 -> 0.88 (after quant)
```
sara: can you paste tokenizer configs for the quantized model vs dataset loader? tokenization mismatches often cause funny prefix matches.
maria: attaching tokenizer.json from model build and dataset tokenization settings (copied). model uses bytepair-v2 with 52k vocab, dataset loader uses our canonical bpe-merge rules. they look similar but token_id mapping differs for some rare tokens.
tim: also check the runner's shard seeding. we had a recent change to continuous batching that accidentally re-seeded RNG per-worker with time() instead of the shard seed — that could duplicate examples across shards.
kevin: ok two hypotheses: 1) token id mapping collision causing truncated prompts to align with holdout answers 2) shard RNG bug duplicates holdout examples across evaluation batches. which matches the logs?
maria: i grepped the raw prediction stream and found the same uid_412 appearing in separate eval shards, different node ids. so duplication is real.
jordan: pinging @ci-bot — are there any CI failures or flaky runs around eval-runner in the last 24h?
ci-bot: recent run 1708205070 failed with: eval-runner:unexpected-duplicates=3. Full artifact: https://ci.internal/runs/1708205070/artifact
sara: small repro patch: add an assertion in the dataset fixture that validates uniqueness of holdout ids before batching. example pytest guard:
```
def test_holdout_uniqueness(holdout_dataset):
    ids = [ex['uid'] for ex in holdout_dataset]
    assert len(ids) == len(set(ids)), f"duplicate ids in holdout: {len(ids)-len(set(ids))}"
```
kevin: nice. also add a runner-level check that stamps each example with a fingerprint that includes (shard_seed, model_variant_hash) so we can detect cross-shard duplicates tied to seed mistakes.
tim: quick SQL I used to detect duplicates in the artifact stream:
```
SELECT uid, count(*) as c FROM predictions WHERE run_id=1708205070 GROUP BY uid HAVING c>1;
```
maria: repro root cause: the model conversion pipeline we used to produce the quantized artifact ran a token remap step to collapse unused ids; the remap wrote a new tokenizer.json but we didn't stage it into the model manifest. eval-runner picked up the old tokenizer from cache while the runtime used the new model vocab -> misaligned token ids. so some short prompts mapped to answer tokens.
kevin: that explains false positives. fix plan:
  - immediate: add pytest guard (sara) and runner duplicate fingerprint (tim)
  - follow-up: ensure model-convert writes manifest.tokenizer_hash and eval-runner verifies model manifest vs loaded tokenizer (maria + eng-runtime)
  - CI: add a gating job that runs a mini-eval comparing tokenized-length-distribution between artifact and dataset for any model onboarding PR
maria: i've pushed a small fix that stages tokenizer.json into the manifest and re-runs conversion. new artifact seems clean locally.
jordan: can we add a lightweight metric to the console: "holdout_dup_rate" per-run and an alert threshold 0.001? ops should get a slack alert.
kevin: yep. i'll file a tracking ticket and assign owners. thanks all.
:sparkles: :thumbsup:
